title: The Batman Part II — Everything We Know About Gotham's Return
excerpt: Robert Pattinson and Matt Reeves are back for The Batman Part II. Confirmed cast, what the first film set up, and which villain is next.
author: StarScoop Daily Staff
imageAlt: The Batman Part II official backdrop — Robert Pattinson returns as Batman
metaDescription: The Batman Part II — confirmed cast, Matt Reeves returning, what the first film set up, and every clue about the sequel's villain.
content:
The Batman did something no other Batman film had managed — it made Gotham feel like a real city with a real crime problem, and it made Batman a detective again rather than a man with gadgets.

The Batman: Part II brings back Robert Pattinson and director Matt Reeves. Here's everything confirmed.

What the First Film Set Up

The 2022 film — currently holding a 7.8 IMDb rating — worked because it refused the usual template. No origin story, no billionaire playboy montage. Just a Batman two years into the job who is not yet good at it, investigating a serial killer through Gotham's institutional rot.

The genre framing was the key decision. This was a detective film — closer to Zodiac or Se7en than to a superhero movie — and it committed to that completely, right down to the pacing.

The ending deliberately left doors open. Gotham was flooded and broken, the city's power structure had been publicly exposed, and Batman's understanding of what the symbol should mean had shifted from vengeance toward something closer to hope.

Crucially, the Riddler ended the film in Arkham, in conversation with an unnamed inmate — a scene widely read as setting up the Joker.

The Confirmed Cast

TMDB currently lists:

  • Robert Pattinson as Bruce Wayne / Batman
  • Jeffrey Wright as Lieutenant James Gordon
  • Andy Serkis as Alfred Pennyworth
  • Colin Farrell as Oswald Cobblepot / The Penguin
  • Jayme Lawson as Bella Reál
  • Scarlett Johansson
  • Sebastian Stan
  • Gil Perez-Abraham

The Johansson and Stan listings are the eye-catching ones — and also the ones to treat most cautiously. Aggregator cast lists get updated ahead of official announcements, and neither role is described. Take those as reported rather than confirmed.

Colin Farrell returning matters most for continuity. His Penguin was unrecognisable under prosthetics and became popular enough to carry a spin-off series, which expanded Gotham's criminal landscape considerably. Part II inherits that groundwork.

Andy Serkis's Alfred is worth noting too — played as a former intelligence operative rather than a butler, which reframed the entire relationship with Bruce.

Which Villain Is Next?

Nothing has been officially confirmed, so here's what the first film actually pointed at rather than speculation dressed as news.

The Joker is the obvious read. The Arkham scene exists specifically to plant him, and the deleted-scene footage Reeves later released showed a heavily scarred version of the character. But Reeves has also been publicly wary of rushing there — the Joker is the most over-used Batman villain in film, and following Heath Ledger and Joaquin Phoenix is an unenviable assignment.

Hush fits the detective format best. It's a mystery story built around an unidentified antagonist, which is exactly the register this series works in.

Mr. Freeze or Clayface would let Reeves keep the grounded tone while introducing something stranger — Freeze in particular has a genuinely tragic core that suits this universe.

Reportedly, Reeves has favoured villains that let the film remain a crime story rather than becoming a spectacle. That instinct argues against a straight Joker film.

Why the Delay Has Been So Long

The gap between films has frustrated fans, and the reasons are mostly structural rather than creative.

Industry-wide production shutdowns pushed nearly every studio schedule. On top of that, DC underwent a full leadership restructure, with a new slate announced under fresh creative direction — and the question of how Reeves's standalone continuity fits alongside a rebooted main DC universe took time to settle.

Reeves also writes slowly and is protective of the script. Given the first film's quality, that's a trade worth accepting.

📽️ Director: Matt Reeves · Studio: Warner Bros. · First film: 2022, IMDb 7.8 · Status: In development

What to Watch For

  • Whether Gotham stays flooded. The first film ended mid-disaster. Picking up in the aftermath would be a bolder choice than a clean reset.
  • Catwoman's return. Selina Kyle left Gotham at the end of the first film. Whether she comes back shapes the emotional core.
  • Tone discipline. The temptation with a sequel is to go bigger. This series works because it stayed small and dirty.

Robert Pattinson is having a notable year — he's also listed in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey and stars opposite Jennifer Lawrence in Die My Love.
